findings.title: Midnight/day helpers de-duplicated into `session_days`
findings.description: `ingest_plan.py` had its own private `_midnight()`; the diff deletes it and reuses the shared `utc_midnight`, and the day-walk loop is now `days_touched()`, reused by `tick_status_build`. This is exactly the "one definition, referenced everywhere" rule, and it keeps the semantics (the `_LAST_INSTANT` microsecond adjustment that keeps a session closing at midnight from touching the next day) in a single place.

findings.title: Exhaustiveness guards keep the status report from silently dropping a bucket
findings.description: `_BUCKET_ROWS` is asserted to cover exactly `set(TickSessionStatus)`, so adding a new member to the enum fails loudly instead of producing a status report that omits it. The same style is used for `EXIT_BY_OUTCOME` in `tick_exit.py`, so the convention is consistent across the slice.

findings.title: The coverage "proof" compares the ledger and the raw rows over different populations
findings.description:
`ledger_totals()` is restricted to the shape's *current* units (`_SHAPE_WHERE`: dataset, symbols, stype_in, stored tiers, `COVERAGE_PREDICATE`), while `raw_counts()` counts **every** row in `tick_trade` whose `ts_event` falls in the session window, with no `unit_id`, shape or product restriction. The comparison in `tick_coverage._session_row` then pairs the two per instrument.

The module docstring's premise — "Raw rows change after commit only through supersession (whose ledger is excluded) or by hand, so a mismatch is evidence of an out-of-band edit or a defect" — does not hold: `adopt` accepts any batch job, and a unit ingested for a *different* shape of the same product (e.g. `symbols = [ESZ4]`, `stype_in = raw_symbol`) writes rows with the same `instrument_id` into `tick_trade`. Those rows are counted as "raw" for the universe's shape but are absent from its ledger, so `mt data tick coverage` would report a mismatch and exit 3 for a database that is in fact consistent. The same asymmetry can mask a real defect if a shape's rows were deleted while another shape's rows keep the count non-zero.

The fix is to scope `raw_counts` to the same units the ledger is scoped to (join through `tick_archive_unit`/`tick_request` with `_SHAPE_WHERE` and `COVERAGE_PREDICATE`, or pass the current unit ids in), so both sides of the proof describe one population.

findings.title: `status`/`coverage` exit 4 when the held days reach the calendar's populated horizon
findings.description:
`_scope` builds its calendar bounds from the held unit days as `utc_midnight(d)` and `utc_midnight(d + 1 day)`, then calls `calendar_sessions(...)` → `TradingCalendar.sessions_between`, which refuses with `OutOfPopulatedRangeError` unless *both* bounds lie inside `[first_open, last_close]` (`trading_calendar.py::_require_populated`).

Two consequences:

* the lower bound `midnight(earliest held day)` is earlier than the calendar's `first_open` when the earliest held unit is the calendar's first session date (that session opens at 22:00, so `midnight` of the same day precedes it);
* the upper bound `midnight(latest held day + 1)` is later than `last_close` whenever the latest held unit is the calendar's last session date — the normal case for an ingest that has caught up to the horizon.

Either case raises `TickCalendarError`, which `exit_code_for` maps to exit 4, so the whole command fails with "calendar … outside populated sessions" instead of reporting the status. This is the same bound rule 225 TD7 established for ingest (`test/unit/data/tick/test_session_days.py`: "ingest's `sessions_between(d, d+1)` never passes the horizon"), where the offending day is instead reported as a per-unit `session_boundary` check failure (`ingest_plan.Calendars.frame`). `build_coverage` widens the same exposure by querying from `utc_midnight(start - timedelta(days=1))`.

Clamping the bounds to the populated span (or intersecting them with the sessions actually held) would keep the verb usable at the edges.

findings.title: The `degraded` count is attached to the wrong bucket line
findings.description:
The bucket rows are appended in a loop over `_BUCKET_ROWS`, and then

```python
lines[-1] += f"   (degraded {p.degraded})"
```

appends the degraded **condition** count to the last bucket line — which is the `edge unknown` row. The output therefore reads `edge unknown 2   (degraded 1)`, which a reader will take as a qualifier of the edge-unknown bucket rather than as the count of degraded days. `degraded` counts sessions whose worst condition is `degraded` (see `tick_status_build._product_status`), which is unrelated to any bucket. It deserves its own line, e.g. `degraded sessions: N`.

findings.title: No load test covers the new bounded `tick_trade` scan
findings.description: The slice adds a read path over the `tick_trade` hypertable (`raw_counts`: a `count(*)` over the range's first open to last close joined against the session array). The project rules require a load test for code on the database/environment paths that asserts on latency, throughput or resource bounds, and the slice already has a load tier (`test/load/test_225_tick_ingest_nfr.py` covers ingest). Nothing exercises `coverage` at scale: a wide `--start/--end` range, a session array with hundreds of entries, or the resulting scan cost on a multi-chunk hypertable is untested. The range is unbounded by the CLI (only `end > start` is checked), so an operator can ask for a decade-wide scan with no statement timeout on the connection.

findings.title: The same shape query is issued twice per product
findings.description: `_scope` calls `shape_units(conn, shape_of(entry))` to learn the held days, and `session_verdicts` calls `shape_units(conn, shape_of(entry))` again for the same shape. The result is identical and the query is not date-bounded, so it reads every unit of the shape twice per product per invocation. Passing the already-fetched map down (or bounding it by day) would halve the work and remove the risk of the two reads disagreeing.

findings.title: Shape matching relies on order-sensitive array equality
findings.description: `Shape.params()` sends `symbols` as the universe's tuple and the predicate compares `r.symbols = %(symbols)s`, which in PostgreSQL is element-wise, order-sensitive array equality. The universe validates that its own symbols are sorted (`universe._validate_entry`), but `tick_request.symbols` is written from the request as adopted/passed. For the single-symbol universe of today this is moot; when slice 231 adds a multi-symbol product whose request was stored in a different order, that unit would silently not match the shape, and `status` would report it as absent rather than held. Sorting on both sides (or comparing as sets) would remove the hazard.

findings.title: Calendar error handling is now implemented twice
findings.description: `calendar_sessions` opens a `TradingCalendar`, calls one method, maps `psycopg.OperationalError` / `CalendarNotFoundError` / `OutOfPopulatedRangeError` to `TickCalendarError` and closes the calendar in a `finally` — the same sequence `tick_calendar.product_session_days` already implements. Two copies of the same exception-to-`TickCalendarError` mapping can drift (as the horizon issue above shows, only one of them was considered). A shared helper in `tick_calendar.py` would keep one definition.

findings.title: The read epilog promises exit 1 for "a setting", but an unset calendar URL exits 4
findings.description: `READ_EPILOG` says exit 1 covers "a setting". An unset `MT_TICK_DB_URL` does exit 1 (`database_url` raises `TickPreflightError`), but an unset `MT_TIMESCALE_DB_URL` — the same class of problem, a missing setting — raises `TickCalendarError` from `calendar_url` and exits 4. The epilog should either name the distinction or the calendar-URL failure should be mapped to the preflight exit.

findings.title: `tick.py`'s docstring no longer names the render modules
findings.description: The docstring still says "Rich rendering lives in `tick_render.py` and `tick_pass_render.py`", but the slice adds `tick_status_render.py` (and `tick_ingest_render.py` already existed). The sentence should mention them, since it is the map a new contributor reads first.

findings.title: The renderer's `age()` helper has no direct test
findings.description: `age()` is pure and has three branches (days, hours, minutes) but is only exercised indirectly through the CLI integration test, which asserts on substrings that do not include the age string. A negative value (a clock skew between the writing host and the reader) would render as `-1h -3m`, which is also untested.
